4. Vocabulary and concept sets

Source: vignettes/book-04-vocabulary.Rmd
book-04-vocabulary.Rmd

What you will learn

Find meanings, look up names and define a reusable concept set.

This chapter uses the synthetic practice connection from Getting started. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Search a name

A concept ID identifies a meaning. It is not a patient’s ID. Search our synthetic vocabulary for education:

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Education", conns = conns)
hits$pooled[c("concept_name", "domain_id", "vocabulary_id")]
#>           concept_name   domain_id vocabulary_id
#> 1   Education question Observation       Fixture
#> 2  Secondary education  Meas Value       Fixture
#> 3 University education  Meas Value       Fixture
#> 4     Education answer  Meas Value       Fixture

This is public vocabulary metadata. We show names in tables throughout the book; numeric IDs occur only in code where they specify what to select.

Look up known answer concepts 

answers <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(900101L, 900102L), conns = conns)
answers$pooled[c("concept_name", "domain_id")]
#>           concept_name  domain_id
#> 1  Secondary education Meas Value
#> 2 University education Meas Value

These are the possible answer meanings in our exercise. Looking them up does not tell you how many people gave either answer.

Include descendants deliberately

A descendant is a more specific meaning below a parent in a vocabulary hierarchy. Our fixture has a small teaching hierarchy with an education-answer parent.

desc <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(900100L, include_self = FALSE, conns = conns)
desc$pooled["concept_name"]
#>           concept_name
#> 1  Secondary education
#> 2 University education

Descendants come from concept_ancestor. Check their clinical meaning before including them; a search result is not automatically a study definition.

Store a set 

education_answers <- omop_concept_set(c(900101L, 900102L))
class(education_answers)
#> [1] "omop_concept_set" "list"

A concept set is a reusable selection of concepts. For the next chapter we need the question set instead. The answer set describes values; it must not replace the question filter in observation_concept_id.

education_question <- omop_concept_set(900001L)
class(education_question)
#> [1] "omop_concept_set" "list"

Both objects are local definitions. Creating one has not selected any patient rows.

Recap

Use IDs to define selections and names to understand them. Question concepts and answer concepts play different roles.

Try it

Look up the two cause-of-death concepts in the fixture and show only their names.

Solution

causes <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(900201L, 900202L), conns = conns)
causes$pooled["concept_name"]
#>            concept_name
#> 1 Myocardial infarction
#> 2             Pneumonia
